title: Jalen Adams' Heave Forces a Fourth Overtime
dek: Down three with 0.8 seconds left in the third overtime, freshman Jalen Adams banked in a three-quarter-court heave — and UConn outlasted Cincinnati 104-97 in four overtimes.

setup.text: UConn came to Orlando with its NCAA tournament hopes on the line. The fifth-seeded Huskies were 21-10 and had lost to Houston and SMU in the final week of the regular season. A loss here, Courant columnist Jeff Jacobs wrote, would in all likelihood have ended any chance at an at-large bid.
Fourth-seeded Cincinnati had NCAA hopes of its own, and it had already beaten UConn twice that season — 58-57 in Hartford and 65-60 at home.

UConn's freshman point guard, Jalen Adams of Roxbury, Mass., had a history with long shots. He won Cushing Academy the 2013 New England prep title with a 35-foot buzzer-beater, hit a half-court shot at UConn's First Night in October, and had spent the previous summer goofing around with absurdly long shots alongside sophomore Daniel Hamilton.

story.text: Cincinnati controlled the first half, leading by as many as 13 and taking a 36-27 lead into the break while UConn shot 35.7 percent. Forward Shonn Miller, in early foul trouble, played only three minutes before halftime.

UConn opened the second half on a 22-9 run and took its first lead since 4-3 on a Hamilton jumper at 13:22. Hamilton's free throws made it 62-55 with 3:36 left — and then UConn did not score again in regulation. Farad Cobb hit a 3 after an Adams turnover, Troy Caupain's two free throws tied it 62-62 with 35 seconds left, and Amida Brimah blocked Caupain's layup at the end to force overtime.

Then the game refused to end. The first overtime ended 67-67 after late 3-point misses by Sterling Gibbs and Caupain. In the second, Cincinnati led by four before two Brimah baskets tied it; Caupain's left-handed hook put the Bearcats ahead with about 15 seconds left, and Adams went coast to coast for a layup that tied it 75-75 with under six seconds to go. Miller fouled out in that overtime.

sequence.text: Caupain, on his way to 37 points, hits a jumper. Cincinnati leads by one.
Hamilton, fouled by Gary Clark, misses the first free throw and makes the second. Tie game.
Caupain misses a 3, but Octavius Ellis grabs the offensive rebound.

Ellis kicks it out to Kevin Johnson, who buries a 3 from the left wing. Cincinnati leads by three with 0.8 seconds left, and the Bearcats celebrate as if they have won — Ellis and Cobb chase Johnson down the floor.

clip.title: K. Johnson made Three Point Jumper. Assisted by O. Ellis.

sequence.text: With the clock stopped, Hamilton and Adams look at each other; each wants the other to take the ball out. Hamilton inbounds it, unchallenged, to Adams on the left side, level with the top of the 3-point arc at the far end.
Clark steps toward Adams, then backs off. Adams turns, brings the ball to his waist, leaps and heaves it two-handed from three-quarter court. It banks off the glass and drops through: 88-88.
UConn's players pour onto the floor and pile on Adams. The officials review the play and rule the ball was out of his hands before the horn. Fourth overtime.
Rodney Purvis fouls out; Ellis makes one of two free throws.
Clark blocks Adams' layup, but Adams grabs his own rebound and scores.
After two Caupain free throws, Adams chases down another offensive rebound, and Gibbs is fouled and makes both. UConn leads for good.
Adams hits a jumper at 2:12 and Hamilton follows with another. UConn leads by five.
Adams makes four free throws in the final 33 seconds, and Hamilton's two at 0:10 finish it. UConn 104, Cincinnati 97.

quotes.text: If it goes in, it would be amazing, and if we lost at least we would go out fighting.
That's legendary stuff to make that shot at that time and just keep performing.
In 0.8 you can't catch the ball, take two steps and then shoot it.
But we thought the game was over too early and he hit a shot that put it into another overtime

aftermath.text: Cronin argued the clock started late and said he felt Cincinnati had won the game; an AAC spokesman called the restarting of the clock a judgment call.

UConn kept going. The next afternoon it beat top-seeded Temple 77-62, and on Sunday it beat Memphis 72-58 for the AAC tournament title, the program's first conference tournament championship since 2011. Hamilton, who had a career-high 32 points, 12 rebounds and eight assists against Cincinnati, was named the tournament's MVP.
Seeded ninth in the NCAA tournament, UConn beat Colorado 74-67 in Des Moines before top-seeded Kansas won 73-61, handing Ollie his first NCAA tournament loss as UConn's coach.

Cincinnati made the NCAA field as a No. 9 seed and lost 78-76 to Saint Joseph's after Octavius Ellis' tying dunk at the buzzer was waved off following a lengthy review — the AP called it the Bearcats' second straight crushing loss.

legacy.text: Jacobs added the shot to UConn's list of unforgettable March shots, alongside Ray Allen's against Georgetown and Taliek Brown's against Pitt — and noted that Allen himself, sitting behind press row, was on his feet with his mouth open.
Only one game in UConn's record-book list of overtime games ran longer: the six-overtime loss to Syracuse in the 2009 Big East quarterfinals.
On the shot's sixth anniversary, in 2022, ESPN posted it on its YouTube channel.
